content:
You are a planning expert. Given an asynchronous planning problem, extract the dependency graph.

For each step, identify:
1. A short snake_case name (e.g., "boil_water", "add_pasta") — use ONLY lowercase letters, digits, and underscores
2. The duration in SECONDS (convert minutes/hours/days if needed: 1 min=60s, 1 hour=3600s, 1 day=86400s)
3. The DIRECT predecessors — steps that MUST complete before this step can start

CRITICAL RULES:
- List ALL direct predecessor steps in "depends_on". A missing dependency will cause a wrong answer.
- If a step has no prerequisites, use an empty list [].
- Every name in "depends_on" MUST exactly match a "name" defined in the same "steps" list.
- Capture ONLY dependencies stated in the problem. Do NOT add extra constraints.

SELF-CHECK before returning:
1. Re-read EVERY ordering constraint in the problem. Is each one captured in some step's "depends_on"?
2. For every entry in any "depends_on" list, confirm that exact name appears as a "name" in the steps list.

Return JSON with key "responses" (list of dicts). Each dict must have key "steps" (list of step dicts).
Each step dict must include:
- "name": snake_case string identifier
- "duration": integer seconds
- "depends_on": list of step name strings (direct predecessors only)

Example:
{
  "responses": [{
    "steps": [
      {"name": "boil_water",  "duration": 300,  "depends_on": []},
      {"name": "add_pasta",   "duration": 600,  "depends_on": ["boil_water"]},
      {"name": "make_sauce",  "duration": 900,  "depends_on": []},
      {"name": "combine",     "duration": 60,   "depends_on": ["add_pasta", "make_sauce"]}
    ]
  }]
}

Here is an asynchronous planning problem.

To beat egg whites, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Check for any yellow yolk specks (30 seconds)
Step 2. Set the speed to medium-high (10 seconds)
Step 3. Observe the formation of soft peaks (120 seconds)
Step 4. Wipe the mixing bowl with lemon juice to remove fat (60 seconds)
Step 5. Take eggs out of the refrigerator (300 seconds)
Step 6. Select a clean copper or glass bowl (45 seconds)
Step 7. Ensure the whisk attachment is bone dry (20 seconds)
Step 8. Incorporate the last of the air (60 seconds)
Step 9. Crack the first egg over a small ramekin (15 seconds)
Step 10. Clear a workspace on the kitchen counter (120 seconds)
Step 11. Measure out the cream of tartar (45 seconds)
Step 12. Plug in the stand mixer (10 seconds)
Step 13. Lower the mixer head into the bowl (5 seconds)
Step 14. Sprinkle the stabilizer over the whites (10 seconds)
Step 15. Wash hands thoroughly with soap (40 seconds)
Step 16. Stop the mixer to check consistency (10 seconds)
Step 17. Set up a "trash" bowl for shells (30 seconds)
Step 18. Adjust the bowl height (15 seconds)
Step 19. Separate the yolk from the white (20 seconds)
Step 20. Add a pinch of fine salt (5 seconds)
Step 21. Monitor the temperature of the whites (60 seconds)
Step 22. Gradually increase the mixer speed (30 seconds)
Step 23. Begin whisking at a low speed (60 seconds)
Step 24. Fetch the egg separator tool (30 seconds)
Step 25. Place the bowl onto the mixer base (10 seconds)
Step 26. Check that the beaters are locked in place (10 seconds)
Step 27. Prepare a second batch of whites if needed (300 seconds)
Step 28. Inspect the bowl for any oily residue (30 seconds)
Step 29. Pour the whites into the main mixing bowl (10 seconds)
Step 30. Get a silicone spatula ready (15 seconds)
Step 31. Locate the superfine sugar (60 seconds)
Step 32. Tap the side of the bowl to settle bubbles (5 seconds)
Step 33. Lock the mixer hinge (5 seconds)
Step 34. Check the bowl for any cracks (20 seconds)
Step 35. Let the eggs sit to reach room temperature (1800 seconds)
Step 36. Remove the mixer splash guard (10 seconds)
Step 37. Position the mixer away from the counter edge (10 seconds)
Step 38. Attach the wire whisk (15 seconds)
Step 39. Rinse the eggshells (20 seconds)
Step 40. Dry the exterior of the eggs (30 seconds)
Step 41. Measure one tablespoon of sugar (30 seconds)
Step 42. Remove any jewelry from hands (60 seconds)
Step 43. Clean up any minor splashes (60 seconds)
Step 44. Read the recipe one last time (120 seconds)
Step 45. Gather a clean metal spoon (20 seconds)
Step 46. Start the motor (5 seconds)
Step 47. Retrieve the carton from the counter (10 seconds)
Step 48. Align the whisk with the center of the bowl (10 seconds)
Step 49. Turn the power dial to 'on' (5 seconds)
Step 50. Select the correct speed setting (10 seconds)
Step 51. Set a kitchen timer for the first interval (15 seconds)
Step 52. Pull back hair or put on an apron (60 seconds)
Step 53. Check for uniform bubble size (30 seconds)
Step 54. Wipe down the whisk wires (30 seconds)
Step 55. Allow the whites to become foamy (60 seconds)
Step 56. Transfer the first white to the mixing bowl (10 seconds)
Step 57. Inspect the whisk for cleanliness (20 seconds)
Step 58. Sift the cream of tartar to remove lumps (60 seconds)
Step 59. Finish the whipping process (180 seconds)
Step 60. Add the cream of tartar to the whites (10 seconds)
Step 61. Listen for the motor pitch to change (30 seconds)
Step 62. Slowly add the sugar one teaspoon at a time (240 seconds)
Step 63. Look for stiff, glossy peaks (60 seconds)
Step 64. Increase speed to maximum (15 seconds)
Step 65. Ensure no water droplets are in the bowl (15 seconds)
Step 66. Double-check the mixer's stability (10 seconds)
Step 67. Sanitize the workspace (180 seconds)
Step 68. Use a magnifying glass to check for yolk (60 seconds)
Step 69. Scrape down the sides of the bowl (20 seconds)
Step 70. Watch for the whites to lose their translucency (60 seconds)
Step 71. Prepare the eggs on a flat surface (20 seconds)
Step 72. Gather all necessary ingredients (120 seconds)
Step 73. Verify the bowl is at room temperature (60 seconds)
Step 74. Turn the mixer to the 'stir' setting (10 seconds)
Step 75. Ensure the eggs are not expired (30 seconds)
Step 76. Open the cream of tartar container (15 seconds)
Step 77. Wipe away a sugar spill (30 seconds)
Step 78. Wait for the bubbles to become very small (120 seconds)
Step 79. Check the freshness of the eggs (60 seconds)
Step 80. Wipe the measuring spoons (20 seconds)
Step 81. Observe the whites turning white (60 seconds)
Step 82. Locate the cream of tartar in the pantry (120 seconds)
Step 83. Find the mixer in the cupboard (60 seconds)
Step 84. Open the sugar canister (15 seconds)
Step 85. Clean the beaters with vinegar (60 seconds)
Step 86. Continue beating until peaks stand straight (120 seconds)
Step 87. Ensure the eggs are large grade (30 seconds)
Step 88. Wipe the counter one more time (45 seconds)
Step 89. Clear the sink of dishes (300 seconds)
Step 90. Wash the sugar measuring cup (60 seconds)
Step 91. Check the texture by rubbing between fingers (10 seconds)
Step 92. Prepare to use the whites immediately (60 seconds)
Step 93. Perform a "bowl inversion" test (10 seconds)
Step 94. Measure the sugar carefully (120 seconds)
Step 95. Sift the sugar (120 seconds)
Step 96. Organize the kitchen tools (300 seconds)
Step 97. Final check for any grease (30 seconds)
Step 98. Set the timer for the final whip (10 seconds)
Step 99. Watch for the trail left by the whisk (60 seconds)
Step 100. Tighten the whisk attachment (15 seconds)
